compiled_state.title: [ci/llm-review]: ci.yml + per-branch-review.yml run duplicate LLM review on story/bug-batch/fix branches -> doubled compute, doubled FP exposure
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** $(git rev-parse HEAD)
* **Affected workflows:** .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/per-branch-review.yml

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

Every line of code that merges to main must pass an LLM code review. Each commit on a story/, bug-batch/, or fix/ branch should receive **exactly one** LLM review per CI cycle — no silent skips (bugs 1624-5fb9, da45-7d92 closed) and no duplicate work.

#### Actual Behavior

Two independent LLM-review pipelines run on every commit on story/, bug-batch/, fix/ branches with an open PR:

| Workflow | Trigger | Job (check name) | In required-checks.txt? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CI` (ci.yml) | pull_request to main | `llm-review` | yes |
| `Sprint Story Review` (per-branch-review.yml) | push to story/**, bug-batch/**, fix/** | `Per-Story LLM Review` | no |

Both jobs invoke the same `plugins/dso/scripts/ci-llm-review-runner.sh`. Both burn API tokens, both produce PR comments, both can produce conflicting verdicts (one pass / one fail) because LLM reviewers are nondeterministic.

Observed on PR #213 (current session):
- Per-Story LLM Review: PASS (no findings)
- llm-review: FAIL (1 important finding — false-positive type-mismatch claim)

The required check is `llm-review`, so the FP gates the PR even though Per-Story LLM Review passed. This structurally amplifies FP risk: two independent reviewer rolls → higher P(at-least-one-FP) than a single roll.

The duplication is also pre-bug-3914-0848-faad-4f6a vestigial. That bug broadened ci.yml's pull_request trigger to fire on PRs targeting any base branch (including session branches). Before that fix, story-branch PRs to session branches skipped ALL of ci.yml — per-branch-review.yml was the only review path. Now that ci.yml covers every PR base, per-branch-review.yml's push trigger is redundant.

### 3. Action History

* bug 1624-5fb9: silent-skip on direct PRs — closed (fail-open defaults added to ci.yml's `changes` job)
* bug da45-7d92: per-branch-review.yml never triggers on sprint commits — closed (sprint orchestrator now creates story/ branches)
* bug 3914-0848-faad-4f6a: ci.yml restricted to PRs targeting main — closed (broadened to any base)

Each fix correctly addressed its symptom but none consolidated the now-redundant per-branch-review.yml.

### 4. Proposed Fix (to be brainstormed)

**Option 1 (preferred — simplest)**: Delete per-branch-review.yml entirely. All review goes through ci.yml's `llm-review` on `pull_request`. Coverage guarantee: every merge goes through merge-to-main-pr.sh which requires the PR to exist, which fires ci.yml's pull_request trigger, which runs llm-review. Single review per commit. No silent skip because the required check is `llm-review` and it must complete.

Risks to verify:
- Does per-branch-review.yml provide ANY coverage that ci.yml does not? Both have the same job set (actionlint, shellcheck, lint-python, test-hooks, test-scripts, validate-required-checks, mirror-defenses-to-pr, llm-review). If any job in per-branch-review.yml has unique configuration (e.g., different gating, different timeout, different dispatch logic), preserve it in ci.yml before deletion.
- Do any branches reach merge WITHOUT a PR? Per merge.strategy=pr + Rule 23 (no direct gh pr merge / git push), no.
- Is there ANY workflow that fires on push to story/bug-batch/fix branches that ISN'T duplicated in ci.yml? If yes, those need a home (could be a separate non-review workflow).

**Option 2 (conservative — preserves push-time review)**: Add an `if:` skip to ci.yml's `llm-review` that fires when the head_ref matches story/**, bug-batch/**, fix/**, AND verifies that per-branch-review.yml has completed successfully on the same SHA. Falls back to running ci.yml's llm-review if the verification fails (no silent skip). More complex but preserves the "review on every push" semantic for sprint flows.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* Affects: .github/workflows/ci.yml (llm-review job), .github/workflows/per-branch-review.yml (entire workflow)
* Reader of required-checks.txt: plugins/dso/scripts/onboarding/provision-ruleset.sh
* Verification: every merged PR over a 1-week sample should show exactly ONE llm-review run per SHA

### 6. Logs

Sample of duplicate runs on PR #213 cycle 1:
- Per-Story LLM Review: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/26012083428/job/76455505768 (PASS)
- llm-review: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/26012083428/job/76455592967 (FAIL)

comments.body:
Implementation analysis (session 2026-05-17, post-PR-#213-merge):

Scope verification — duplication is not just LLM review. `gh pr checks 213` showed both `Script Tests` (per-branch-review.yml: failed intermittently) and `Script Tests` (ci.yml: passed) on the same commit. The full overlap set between per-branch-review.yml and ci.yml:

| per-branch-review.yml job | ci.yml job | Functionally equivalent? |
|---|---|---|
| actionlint | actionlint | yes |
| shellcheck | shellcheck | yes |
| lint-python | lint-python | yes |
| test-hooks | test-hooks | yes |
| test-scripts | test-scripts | yes |
| validate-required-checks | validate-required-checks | yes |
| mirror-tracker-defenses | mirror-defenses-to-pr | yes (job name differs, script call is the same) |
| review (Per-Story LLM Review) | llm-review | yes (both call ci-llm-review-runner.sh) |

ci.yml has one extra job (`changes` for paths filtering). Nothing in per-branch-review.yml is unique to it.

merge-to-main-pr.sh enforcement: parses required-checks.txt, polls `gh pr checks` and requires SUCCESS conclusion for every listed check — SKIPPED and NEUTRAL are explicitly rejected (per source comment: 'branch protection rules may treat them as not-passing-required'). This rules out the cheap fix of adding job-level `if:` skips on ci.yml's overlapping jobs.

Three implementation paths:

**Option A — delete per-branch-review.yml, rely entirely on ci.yml's pull_request trigger.** Justified by merge.strategy=pr (every line that gets MERGED has a PR, ci.yml fires on every PR). Loss: push-time early feedback during sprint iterations (acceptable per user priority: 'every line that gets MERGED has passed an LLM review' — merge-time, not push-time). Required downstream cleanup: 4 files (migrate-story-pr-bases.sh dead invocation, INSTALL.md 6 refs, CI-INTEGRATION.md 3 refs, CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md 2 refs); 2 likely-now-unreferenced helpers (resolve-per-branch-review-base.sh, assert-batch-branch.sh comments).

**Option B — keep both workflows, add delegation-verify on ci.yml's overlapping jobs.** Each overlapping ci.yml job becomes a thin shim that on covered branches (story/, bug-batch/, fix/) waits for per-branch-review.yml's corresponding check to complete on the same SHA. Success → exit 0 (job conclusion=success, no SKIPPED problem). Failure or timeout → exit 1 (no silent skip). Preserves push-time feedback. Cost: ~30 lines added per overlapping job in ci.yml (~8 jobs); polling loop with timeout; meaningful complexity.

**Option C — brainstorm via /dso:brainstorm.** Defer the design decision (push-feedback vs single source of truth) and consuming-project impact assessment to a proper session.

Maintainer direction (2026-05-17 session): no decision made yet — they asked for the analysis attached to this ticket before choosing. Pending input on A vs B vs C.

Side benefit of either A or B: removes the FP-amplifier effect documented in this ticket's original report (PR #213 saw llm-review fail with an int-vs-string FP while Per-Story LLM Review passed on the same commit — two independent rolls compound the per-commit FP rate).

comments.body:
## Resolution decision — moved to epic b575

This bug describes a structural duplication that is on-scope for epic b575-ac1c-f720-4839 ("Cycle-end arbiter + workflow unification (BLOCK/DEFER/DROP rulings, max_cycles, parity local+PR)"), not an orthogonal CI cleanup. Two PR-side workflows running ci-llm-review-runner.sh against the same SHA break several epic invariants:

- cycle-ledger integrity (story 5621 will wire runner.py to write cycle-ledger.json → two ledger entries per SHA → cycle_num and cross_cycle_pattern undefined)
- arbiter dispatch dedup (cycle-end arbiter already on main from story b1b6) — duplicate dispatch yields duplicate orphan-task tickets and duplicate defense-store rows
- review.max_cycles enforcement (story 35b8, merged) — effective cap becomes 2 * max_cycles
- SC10 E2E PR validation (story c4f1) — "the arbiter fired on a real PR" is ambiguous when two runs exist
- Parity local+PR (epic SC) — local has 1 entry point (/dso:commit → /dso:review); PR currently has 2

Decision: rather than fixing this as a standalone bug, the work is captured as a new story under epic b575, slotted between story 35b8 (max_cycles config, closed) and story 5621 (CI runner wiring). 5621 depends_on this new story so its cycle-ledger writes land on a single canonical PR-side pipeline.

The required check stays `llm-review` per required-checks.txt; the branch ruleset still enforces it; coverage of "no merge without LLM review" is preserved mathematically (the canonical run is the same — we only remove the duplicate run, not the required run).

Closing this bug as MOVED — work tracked under the new story (linked below).
